rule: THE CLOSED CONNECTOR VOCABULARY (bim-core-5 + cabling-1). A port's `connector` is one of these ids; every other spelling is an alias of exactly one id. An importer stores the id and keeps the original text in `connector_as_declared`.

Each entry carries its ISO 16739 port words: Pset_DistributionPortTypeCable.ElectricalConnectionType (enum), ConnectionSubtype (= `subtype`, the house name), ConnectionGender (enum: the PINS' gender, so an IEC C14 inlet is MALE) and, where one conductor is named, ConductorFunction. `pins` is APK_Terminal.PinCount; `pinout` the default APK_Terminal.Pinout in pin order (the part's own wins); `conductors` the ConductorFunction of each mains pin.

Most AV connectors have no ISO word (speakON, Euroblock, fibre, SFP, EDAC): ElectricalConnectionType OTHER, and ConnectionSubtype is the TRADE name the industry says (speakON NL4, Phoenix 3.5 mm 3-pin, LC duplex, opticalCON DUO); the generic names (Euroblock 3-pin, 3.5 mm pitch; Neutrik speakON NL4; terminal block) are aliases (owner, ROAD-3598 answer 14, 2026-11-06). Mains connectors are ACPLUG, DC barrels and batteries DCPLUG.

`placeholder: true` marks an importer word that names no connector (Jack, Video, Data, '8-pin connector'): it resolves, NOTKNOWN, and is counted apart in the census. An unknown spelling resolves to nothing and goes into the census; it is never silently OTHER.
Lookup: normalise (below), try the whole text, then the text with trailing parentheticals removed; failing that split on ' / ' and ';' and resolve each part (a port that offers two connectors).
Gender words: P / plug / male / M = MALE; S / socket / jack / receptacle / R (NEMA) / female / F = FEMALE. An entry with no stated gender is NOTKNOWN.

`presentation` is how a gender is SHOWN to a person: PLUG for MALE, SOCKET for FEMALE; every other gender (OTHER, NOTKNOWN, UNSET) shows NOTKNOWN (owner, ROAD-3598 answer 16, 2026-11-06). ConnectionGender stays the IFC word in every file; PLUG / SOCKET is never written to IFC.

`source` {document, url, pages, note}: the maker's document an entry's words were read from (a combo may carry one too). An entry that cites one claims nothing that document does not say: what it leaves open stays NOTKNOWN / null.

`domain_aliases` {domain: [spelling]}: a spelling that names a different connector on a port of that domain (contracts part DOMAINS). '3.5 mm male' is the TRS jack on an audio port and the precision APC-3.5 coaxial on an rf port, so it is a plain alias of TRS-3.5-M and an rf alias of COAX-APC-3.5-M. A reader given the port's domain tries that domain's aliases first, then the plain ones; without a domain only the plain ones count. A spelling is a domain alias of at most one id per domain.

`combos`: one declared spelling that names two connectors at once with no ' / ' between them (an adapter: '3-pin WE/XLR Adapter' is the Western Electric socket and the XLR it adapts to). It resolves to its `ids` in order, exactly as their ' / ' combo does; a combo spelling is never also an alias.
normalise: Curly double quotes and the double prime become '"'; en dash, em dash and minus sign become '-'.
A number followed by optional spaces and 'mm' becomes '<n> mm'; a number followed by optional spaces and 'inch'/'inches' becomes '<n>"'.
Runs of white space become one space; leading/trailing space and trailing - , ; : . are removed.

The HP/Agilent/Keysight 34420A nanovoltmeter's front INPUT, as Keysight's user's guide draws it: four almost-pure-copper contacts, keyed, a coupling nut; the connector body and cable shield are earth. Channel 1 HI / LO: DCV + / -, 4-wire ohms Source + / -, 2-wire ohms and thermistor Source and Sense + / -. Channel 2 HI / LO: DCV + / -, 4-wire ohms Sense + / -, thermocouple + / -. The guide numbers no pins, so the pinout is in channel order. It names no gender (p. 305 draws two raised and two recessed contacts on the front panel), so ConnectionGender stays NOTKNOWN. Mates the 34102A low-thermal cable, the 34103A 4-wire shorting plug and the 34104A blank connector (p. 308). Not a LEMO entry: the guide names no maker family.

The Western Electric 618A's own connector: the fixed 405A jack built into the microphone, mating the 285A cord plug (284A / 286A / 286B are the fixed plugs). Compression contacts closed by the plug's cam lever. The bulletin states no contact count (WE's 1931 sales booklet speaks of three prongs on the housing; the instruction bulletin's jack is what is declared), so pins stay null.

source.document: Western Electric, Moving Coil Type Microphone No. 618A and Associated Apparatus, Instructions for Use
source.note: Bulletin pages [3]-[5] (PDF pages 4-6): 'The No. 405A Jack is of the fixed mounted type and is designed to mount as a part of the No. 618A Microphone'; the 285A plug on the cord engages it and its cam lever presses the compression contacts; 'The plug of the cord being used should be inserted in the jack forming part of the microphone' (Figure 5, Plugs and Jacks).
